summary: The codebase is a solid foundation for an agent-based simulation of mask adoption dynamics with modular design and improved robustness compared to prior iterations. However, the simulation currently does not run (empty main()), and it diverges from the task spec in several key areas: missing/incorrect evaluation metrics, incomplete parameter normalization/usage (e.g., enforcement_probability, campaign_frequency_days, restock_period_days, supply_delay_days), and incorrect inequality computation. There are also logic gaps (mandate activation requires both start and end), performance issues (O(n) lookups in free distribution), and minor inconsistencies (metric names). Addressing these issues will make the simulation executable, compliant with the spec, and more realistic.

critical_issues.issue: Empty main() prevents the simulation from running
critical_issues.impact: No results are produced; verification and evaluation cannot proceed
critical_issues.solution: Implement main() to instantiate Simulation(MODEL_PLAN), run the simulation, evaluate metrics, and optionally visualize/save results

critical_issues.issue: Missing or misaligned evaluation metrics vs spec (policy_compliance_rate, mask_availability, price_level, adoption_inequality_by_income, time_to_50pct_adoption naming)
critical_issues.impact: Key outputs required by the spec are absent or misnamed, preventing correct evaluation and downstream analysis
critical_issues.solution: Compute and expose: (1) policy_compliance_rate restricted to required-policy visits; (2) mask_availability as average inventory and stockout frequency; (3) price_level as average price over time; (4) adoption_inequality_by_income using top/bottom income quantiles; (5) add time_to_50pct_adoption alias

critical_issues.issue: Mandate activation logic requires both start and end days
critical_issues.impact: Cannot model start-only mandates or respect mandate_active_initial; reduces policy realism and prevents configurations common in the spec
critical_issues.solution: Support: mandate_active_initial, start-only activation (active from start forward), and optional end day. Fall back to defaults when missing

critical_issues.issue: Spec parameters not normalized or used (enforcement_probability, campaign_frequency_days, restock_period_days, supply_delay_days, location_mask_requirement_default, purchase_threshold_price_sensitivity)
critical_issues.impact: Behavior deviates from the specification; e.g., policy enforcement is not probabilistic, campaigns aren’t periodic, market supply dynamics are too simplistic, and purchasing does not include price sensitivity threshold
critical_issues.solution: Normalize these parameters in _normalize_params and implement them in PolicyCampaignModule, InformationChannelModule, RetailerSupplyModule, and BehaviorDecisionModule

critical_issues.issue: Adoption inequality computed by SES quintile instead of income quantiles
critical_issues.impact: The inequality metric doesn’t match the spec and can misrepresent disparities
critical_issues.solution: Compute the difference in adoption rates between top and bottom income quantiles (e.g., top 20% vs bottom 20%) and expose it as adoption_inequality_by_income

critical_issues.issue: policy_compliance_rate logic not aligned with spec
critical_issues.impact: Reported compliance doesn’t reflect mandate-required compliance by visits and can be misleading
critical_issues.solution: Calculate compliance strictly for locations where mask_policy == 'required', weighted by number of attendees (visits)

critical_issues.impact: Lost opportunity to analyze contact exposure; can break any downstream logic dependent on contact counts
critical_issues.solution: After contact generation, write contacts_per_agent back to agents’ daily_contacts

critical_issues.issue: O(n) agent lookup in free mask distribution loop
critical_issues.solution: Use an id_to_agent map for O(1) lookup in PolicyCampaignModule.update()

critical_issues.issue: Spec weights (social_influence_weight, authority_trust_weight, risk_signal_level, decision_noise) are not mapped
critical_issues.impact: Differences between specified and implemented decision logic can skew adoption dynamics and calibration
critical_issues.solution: Map spec weights to internal weights in BehaviorDecisionModule.update(): social_influence_weight -> peer_influence_weight, authority_trust_weight -> trust_weight, risk_signal_level -> multiplicative modifier of utility, decision_noise -> adoption_noise

model_improvements.current_approach: Deterministic enforcement based on enforcement_level; mandate activation requires both start and end
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Introduce enforcement_probability to gate enforcement events; allow start-only mandates and mandate_active_initial; maintain default location policies per spec
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Closer adherence to policy scenarios; more realistic compliance responses

model_improvements.suggested_approach: Use campaign_frequency_days to spike media influence on schedule; optionally decay between campaigns
model_improvements.expected_benefit: More realistic temporal variation in public messaging and effects

model_improvements.suggested_approach: Implement restock_period_days and supply_delay_days via a delivery queue; compute mask_availability as avg inventory and stockout days
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Better capture of supply constraints and their impacts on adoption

model_improvements.current_approach: Price elasticity applied to quantity only
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Add a purchase_threshold_price_sensitivity that reduces intent probability when expected price is high relative to income; map spec weights to decision components
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Improved heterogeneity and income-based disparities in adoption

model_improvements.suggested_approach: Compute adoption_inequality_by_income using top/bottom income quantiles
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Alignment with spec and more precise measurement of economic inequality effects

code_improvements.modification: Implement main() to run the simulation and report metrics
code_improvements.reason: Current main() is empty; the simulation never executes

code_improvements.modification: Allow mandates with only a start day and support mandate_active_initial; implement enforcement_probability; use location_mask_requirement_default for non-mandate periods
code_improvements.reason: Align with spec and support common policy scenarios

code_improvements.modification: Introduce campaign_frequency_days to modulate media_signal on specific days
Add restock_period_days and supply_delay_days via a restock queue; compute and expose avg inventory and stockout counts
code_improvements.reason: Align with market dynamics in the spec and provide mask_availability

code_improvements.modification: Map spec weights to internal; add purchase_threshold_price_sensitivity to gating of intents; use risk_signal_level and decision_noise
code_improvements.reason: Improve behavioral realism and spec alignment

code_improvements.modification: Write contacts_per_agent to each agent’s daily_contacts; keep a count of required-policy visits and compliant visits
code_improvements.reason: Track individual contact exposure and support policy_compliance_rate metric

code_improvements.modification: Add policy_compliance_rate, mask_availability (avg inventory and stockout_rate), price_level time series, adoption_inequality_by_income (quantiles), and alias time_to_50pct_adoption
code_improvements.reason: Expose required metrics with proper naming and definitions

code_improvements.modification: Replace next(...) linear lookup with id_to_agent map for free mask distribution
code_improvements.reason: Avoid O(n) scan per recipient to improve performance

code_improvements.modification: Normalize spec parameter names (enforcement_probability, campaign_frequency_days, restock_period_days, supply_delay_days, location_mask_requirement_default, purchase_threshold_price_sensitivity) to internal keys
code_improvements.reason: Ensure parameters from spec are usable throughout modules

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Attitudes and utility weights are not fully mapped to spec; media and policy timing are static
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Calibrate peer_influence_weight, trust_weight, and risk_perception_weight against observed adoption curves; add periodic campaigns and start-only mandates to match historical sequences

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Not restricted to required-policy visits; no enforcement_probability
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Compute visit-weighted compliance only at required locations and parameterize enforcement_probability based on observed inspection frequencies

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Only a binary stock indicator per retailer/day is used
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Track and report avg inventory and stockout_rate; calibrate restock_period_days and supply_delay_days from supplier lead-time distributions
Use income data to create quantiles; validate against observed adoption disparities by income (e.g., survey data)

prioritized_actions: Implement main() to execute the simulation and print/save key metrics
Add and expose all required evaluation metrics with correct definitions and names
Fix mandate activation logic to support start-only and mandate_active_initial; add enforcement_probability
Normalize and implement spec parameters (campaign_frequency_days, restock_period_days, supply_delay_days, purchase_threshold_price_sensitivity)
Write daily_contacts and policy-compliant visits for accurate compliance metrics
Optimize free mask distribution lookups with id_to_agent
additional_comments: The module ordering, O(1) lookups, neighbor mapping, and price elasticity are all positive developments. Visualization is guarded appropriately for headless environments. Consider adding a lightweight unit test harness for core modules (network building, policy toggle logic, retailer restock queue) and a small population smoke test to catch future regressions. Also, documenting the mapping between spec and internal parameters would aid maintainability.

change_analysis.summary: The recent changes improve structural robustness and feature coverage: neighbor mapping is now by agent IDs, there’s a cap on contacts with workplace multiplier, price elasticity is added, and aggregator gains several metrics. However, main() is now empty, mandate activation became too restrictive (requires both start and end), and required spec metrics remain missing or misnamed.
positive_impacts: Network neighbor mapping no longer assumes ID == index
Adherence and fatigue dynamics make behavior more realistic
Retail pricing uses price elasticity and scarcity markup
Additional aggregated metrics (masked_interaction_fraction, supply adequacy, adherence) were added
negative_impacts: Mandate logic requires both start and end dates, reducing flexibility
Spec-specified metrics still not fully aligned or exposed
Policy enforcement lacks enforcement_probability and periodic campaigns
suggestions: Implement main() immediately to enable execution
Relax mandate activation logic and support mandate_active_initial
Add spec metrics and parameter normalization as outlined
Introduce restock queue with supply delay and campaign frequencies for more realistic dynamics
